messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty triggered — elevated 502/504 rate on api-gateway-prod. error_rate=8.2% (5m), p95=1.2s, severity=SEV2. See https://redwood.grafana.net/d/alerts/incident/6378912345
oncall-sre: Oncall stepping in, paging corridor. Assigning @maya @liam to triage.
maya: looking at grafana now — spike seems concentrated to eu-west mux cluster (mux-eu-03). latency and 5xx both up on that shard.
liam: any recent deploys or config changes?
eng-runtime: no model/runtime deploys in last 30m. there was a routing policy change ~23m ago increasing fanout to mux-eu-* for A/B traffic.
maya: that timing aligns. i can shift traffic to eu-fallback pool (eu-fallback-01) to relieve mux-eu-03. proposing quick 30% shift to measure impact.
ops-runner: traffic shift command (use with care):
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/route/update -d '{"service":"api-gateway","weights":{"mux-eu":70,"eu-fallback":30}}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```
support-jordan: support intake: ~12 customers reported 5xx in last 10m, two high-touch customers: AtlassianX, RetailCorp. open tickets: #3456, #3457.
oncall-sre: Start shift now. @product-alex FYI for customer comms.
incident-bot: Action recorded — traffic shift started by maya at +00:02. new weights: mux-eu 70% -> eu-fallback 30%.
maya: applied the weight change, watching errors.
incident-bot: Update +00:05: error rate down to 4.9% (≈40% improvement). p95 latency -> 900ms.
liam: good improvement. need root cause — maya can you pull mux-eu-03 logs and look for upstream errors / cache complaints: `kubectl logs mux-eu-03 -n prod --since=15m`
maya: tail shows repeated entries: 
```
[2026-03-17T00:12:03Z] mux-eu-03 | ERROR | upstream read timeout for backend=edge-proxy-eu-1 status=502
[2026-03-17T00:12:04Z] mux-eu-03 | WARN  | kvcache: eviction spike, free=4MB, threshold=8MB
[2026-03-17T00:12:05Z] mux-eu-03 | ERROR | http: response 502 to client id=xyz
```
eng-runtime: looks like KV cache exhaustion + upstream timeouts on mux-eu-03. GC spikes reported in node metrics around same time. likely routing change increased concurrency and pushed cache beyond limits.
liam: mitigation options: 1) enforce temporary connection limit on mux-eu-03, 2) accelerate rolling update to apply memory GC tunables, 3) keep traffic shifted until we stabilize.
ops-runner: i'll push a conservative connection cap to mux-eu-03 cluster: `--max-connections=1200` and start a rolling restart.
incident-bot: Rolling restart initiated by ops-runner. expected pod churn ~2m/pod.
maya: after first pod restart metrics show errors still present but trending down.
incident-bot: Update +00:12: error rate 2.1%, p95=600ms. customer failures reduced.
support-jordan: sending interim note to AtlassianX & RetailCorp: "We're seeing reduced failures after mitigation; we'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full resolution."
product-alex: appreciate the quick mitigation. please capture routing change as likely contributing factor in postmortem.
oncall-sre: Handoff plan: I'll remain until stable for another 30m, then hand to night oncall @liam. Summary for handoff channel: degraded -> mitigated, ongoing investigation.
maya: short summary: root-cause hypothesis = routing fanout increase + kv-cache GC/exhaustion on mux-eu-03 causing upstream read timeouts -> 502/504. Mitigations applied: 1) traffic shifted to eu-fallback pool, 2) connection cap applied, 3) rolling restarts to pick up GC tunables. Next steps: reproduce in staging, review routing policy rollout process, add runbook entry for mux kvcache limits.
liam: taking next oncall shift. will continue log correlation and postmortem draft. please add 'mux kvcache GC/conn limits' to runbook.
incident-bot: Incident paging closed. postmortem draft seeded: https://redwood.incidents/6378912345-draft.md
